body: Quality (business + management), Growth, Longevity, Price (+Size). 100x study: ~47/3,500 stocks did 100x in ~12 yrs; small size at start. 8/10 fastest 2016–21 started < ₹2,000 cr mcap.
title: Motilal Oswal QGLP / SQGLP

body: As taught in Bakshi's public lectures and blog: (1) Identify businesses with durable moats - pricing power, switching costs, network effects, cost advantages, brands, regulatory licences - evidenced by stable high ROCE. (2) Wait for 'bad news' that is temporary or non-structural: a regulatory scare, a one-off loss, an industry panic, a management change misread by the market. (3) Separate temporary from permanent: does the bad news damage the moat, or only this year's earnings? (4) Use behavioural finance to exploit overreaction (loss aversion, recency bias) and to check one's own biases. (5) Prefer 'clean surprises': hidden strengths that later show up in reported numbers. Indian examples of the pattern (not his holdings): high-quality lenders after one-off asset-quality scares, consumer franchises during temporary input-cost spikes. Risk: misjudging a permanent moat break (technology disruption, regulation) as temporary.
title: Bakshi: moats bought on temporary bad news
